correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs both weighted level-set definitions and their p=1 normalization. Chen--Yang--Yuan--Zhang Lemma 2.5 independently verifies the base D(U) estimate. The new O(U) estimate is proved via small near-tip scales (section measure dr/r), an integrable derivative envelope off-tip, and a compact-support large-radius bound. A bounded Phi(s)/s and the explicit local derivative assumption imply global Lipschitz continuity, so both weak tests inherit finite values. Converse pair and two-subinterval tests each yield a quantified Phi(s)/s lower bound along arbitrary divergent ratio sequences. The W1,1 claim follows by piecewise monotone absolutely-continuous composition and matching endpoints; no finite computation is misused.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches for both arXiv IDs, the weak gamma=-1 BSVY quotient, the Frank mean oscillation test, the nonlinear cusp envelope and the two-scale boundary returned no statement covering both exact equivalences. The inspected published mathematical records contain no result asserting this joint endpoint profile theorem. The closest published BSVY Sobolev/BV separation proves a different strict inclusion; log-monotone Marcinkiewicz results concern different objects. Chen et al Lemma 2.5 supplies D(U)<infinity, and Lemma 3.10 supplies a partial lower weak-L1 log-coordinate mechanism, not O(U) or the joint equivalence. Frank Proposition 4 establishes divergence for alpha<1 and lacks a positive threshold or general Phi criterion. Brezis et al Theorem 1.1 describes generic exceptional p=1 behavior, not the composition-cone classification. The exact phase for alpha=1, beta>=0 and full regular outer profiles is not implied by any inspected statement.

value.rationale: The two natural derivative-free weak endpoint tests in current functional analysis are not equivalent to generic W1,1 membership. On the source-defined logarithmic cusp cone, this gives a genuine necessary-and-sufficient structural criterion, not just one more failing example: boundedness of Phi(s)/s simultaneously characterizes both distributions, and the exact alpha=1 loglog boundary cleanly separates continuous W1,1 functions with finite and infinite tests. The cone is infinite-dimensional, the quantitative logarithmic mechanism is explicit, and the joint criterion is a motivated reusable benchmark for endpoint theories. No paper-sized extension, universal equivalence, or numerical constant is falsely promised.
